description: Add admin-only data backup download at GET /admin/backup. Creates a new backupController.js that fetches all Firestore collections (events + per-event sub-collections) and streams them as a JSON attachment. Add 'Download Backup' button to the Quick Actions section of views/dashboard/admin.xian. Independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.
steps: Step 1 — Create controllers/backupController.js. Use ESM: import { db } from '../models/firebaseConfig.js'; import { collection, getDocs, getDoc, doc } from 'firebase/firestore'; Export: export const backupData = async (req, res) => { try { ... } catch(err) { console.error(err); res.status(500).json({ error: 'Backup failed.' }); } };

Step 2 — Inside backupData, fetch all events: const eventsSnap = await getDocs(collection(db, 'events')); Build array: const eventsData = []; for (const evDoc of eventsSnap.docs) { const evObj = { id: evDoc.id, ...evDoc.data() }; // fetch sub-collections in parallel const [contestants, criteria, scores, auditLog] = await Promise.all([ getDocs(collection(db, 'events', evDoc.id, 'contestants')), getDocs(collection(db, 'events', evDoc.id, 'criteria')), getDocs(collection(db, 'events', evDoc.id, 'scores')), getDocs(collection(db, 'events', evDoc.id, 'audit_log')) ]); evObj.contestants = contestants.docs.map(d => ({ id: d.id, ...d.data() })); evObj.criteria = criteria.docs.map(d => ({ id: d.id, ...d.data() })); evObj.scores = scores.docs.map(d => ({ id: d.id, ...d.data() })); evObj.audit_log = auditLog.docs.map(d => ({ id: d.id, ...d.data() })); eventsData.push(evObj); }
Step 3 — Inside backupData, fetch users collection: const usersSnap = await getDocs(collection(db, 'users')); const usersData = usersSnap.docs.map(d => ({ id: d.id, ...d.data() }));

Step 4 — Build the backup object and send: const date = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]; const backup = { exportedAt: new Date().toISOString(), exportedBy: req.session.userName || 'admin', version: '1.0', events: eventsData, users: usersData }; res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json'); res.setHeader('Content-Disposition', 'attachment; filename=scoresync-backup-' + date + '.json'); return res.status(200).send(JSON.stringify(backup, null, 2));

Step 5 — Add route in routes/index.js. Add at top with other admin imports: import { backupData } from '../controllers/backupController.js'; Add route after the /users routes block (admin section): router.get('/admin/backup', requireAuth, requireRole('admin'), backupData);

Step 6 — Add 'Download Backup' button in views/dashboard/admin.xian Quick Actions section. Insert after the Analytics action link and before the closing of the p-3 space-y-1 container. Use the same link-row pattern as the existing quick actions:
Download Backup
Full JSON export
acceptance_criteria: GET /admin/backup returns 302 to /login when not authenticated
GET /admin/backup returns 200 with Content-Type application/json and Content-Disposition attachment filename=scoresync-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json for admin
The downloaded JSON contains top-level keys: exportedAt, exportedBy, version, events, users
Each event entry in the JSON contains sub-arrays: contestants, criteria, scores, audit_log
'Download Backup' link appears in the Quick Actions section of the admin dashboard
verification: Start server, log in as admin, click 'Download Backup' in admin dashboard Quick Actions, confirm browser downloads a .json file with the correct filename and correct structure
findings: Implemented all steps. controllers/backupController.js created with ESM imports; fetches events + sub-collections (contestants, criteria, scores, audit_log) and users collection, then streams JSON attachment. Route GET /admin/backup added to routes/index.js protected by requireAuth + requireRole('admin'). Download Backup link added as fifth Quick Action in views/dashboard/admin.xian using teal gradient icon matching existing link-row pattern. Both JS files pass node --check with no syntax errors.
